question.knowledge_point: Identifying Values in the Domain of the Inverse Tangent Function
question.problem:
Which of the following values lies in the domain of $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x?$

I. $\frac{\pi }{3}$

II. $2\pi $

III. $-\frac{\pi }{6}$
question.worked_solution:
Let's recall the graph of $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13963369/assets/6860bcf04c508b0abe795b9e1699163ac9495818f6427b338ac6bbe17774b2d8.png)

Note that:

- The function is defined for all real numbers.

Therefore, all the given values are in the domain of $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x.$

judgment.reasoning: The earlier answers remain correct, and each agrees with its own captured worked solution. q-123715: all three sequences tend to 0 because logarithms grow more slowly than positive powers and exponentials grow faster than powers. The source names a_n, b_n, and c_n, corresponding respectively to I, II, and III. q-65828: only III satisfies x=cos(y) with 0≤y≤π; I has x=π/3>1, and II has y=7π/4>π. q-70769: only I satisfies those conditions; II has negative y, and III fails because cos(π/3)=1/2 rather than 1. q-70777 and q-117329: arctan is defined for every real number, so all three listed values qualify in each question.
